gates.reason: Checked the test's temporary filesystem isolation and its authn, CSRF-origin, content-type, body-size, and non-loopback rejection cases; no current defect found.
This is a route regression test, not detector, parser, calculation, recommendation, or validated-fix production code.
This standalone regression test is not hot-path or shipped request-processing code.
The orchestrator executes a fixture-provided gate command through an unjailed host shell; cwd is not a filesystem, network, or secret boundary.
The script emits causal-proof claims after deleting run artifacts and omits the per-run measurements and outcomes needed to reproduce the aggregates.
Concurrent workers buffer unbounded stdout and stderr and repeatedly rebuild large strings/arrays before parsing.

findings.title: Fixture gate commands execute in an unjailed host shell
findings.what: runGate passes gate.command to `bash -c` on the host. Setting cwd to a throwaway tree does not prevent the command from reading home-directory secrets, writing elsewhere, accessing the network, or spawning arbitrary processes. This bypasses the mandatory jail applied only to model workers.
findings.fix: Execute objective gates through the same mandatory sandbox with a minimal environment and explicit read/write mounts, or replace free-form shell commands with a closed, argument-based verifier allowlist.
findings.acceptance: A fixture gate attempting to read a marker outside its materialized tree, write outside that tree, or access the network is denied, while existing deterministic gates still run successfully.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that lines 279-282 directly execute the bundle-derived command as `bash -c`; lines 270-272 explicitly state it is unjailed, and no confinement beyond cwd is applied.

findings.title: Proof receipts discard the run-level evidence required to reproduce their claims
findings.what: Per-run costs, gate outcomes, unresolved states, token counts, and worker-result provenance exist only in memory and their scratch artifacts are deleted immediately. The emitted receipt records aggregate deltas and objective command strings but not the underlying observations, so its causal recommendation and projection cannot be independently re-derived from the persisted artifact.
findings.fix: Persist a structured evidence artifact containing each pair/arm/run identifier, gate outcome, cost value and source, token counts, model, timestamps, and artifact digest; reference that immutable artifact and its digest from the receipt before cleanup.
findings.acceptance: Given only a finalized receipt and its referenced evidence artifact, an independent checker can recompute nDecided, success rates, medians, confidence interval, Wilcoxon result, verdict, and projection exactly, and verify the artifact digest.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass confirmed runs are cleaned at lines 499-503 and the receipt built at lines 675-700 contains only fixture/gate references and aggregates, with no run-level measurements or artifact digest.

findings.title: Concurrent worker output is buffered without a size limit
findings.what: Each worker appends all stdout and stderr to strings without a cap, then splits, trims, filters, and parses the complete stdout again. With concurrent verbose stream-json workers, memory grows with total output and repeated string concatenation/copying can add substantial latency or exhaust the orchestrator.
findings.fix: Parse NDJSON incrementally, retain only the final result and adherence counters, keep a bounded stderr tail, and terminate or mark unresolved when a documented per-worker output budget is exceeded.
findings.acceptance: A probe feeding output beyond the configured worker-output budget keeps process memory within the stated bound, returns a controlled unresolved result, and normal worker output still yields the same cost and stable-read values.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed both streams accumulate without bounds at lines 225-228 and the full stdout is duplicated and reparsed at lines 240-260; concurrency allows several such buffers simultaneously.
